4.2 Cylinders manufactured in accordance with approved specifications shall be provided with an It shall be borne in mind that additional wall thickness to allow for corrosion during service. corrosion is not related to the thickness of the container so that any additional thickness allowed for corrosion should be constant rather than a given proportion of thickness. 4.3 Further additional wall thickness shall also be considered necessary in order that the cylinder can safely withstand stresses due to horizontal acceleration and retardation in normal road transportation. The cylinder shall be so designed that the maximum permissible equivalent stress will not be exceeded when the stresses in the cylinder due to vertical accelerations are superimposed The vertical accelerations considered should be those upon the stress due to internal pressure. Disposal of Condemned Cylinders

6.1 Cylinders which do not comply with the requirements of inspection and testing shall be destroyed in accordance with IS : 9200-I 979 <Methods of disposal of unserviceable compressed gas cylinders'. 6.2 Record of such cylinders 7. Fittings 7.1 Cylinders shall be fitted with a valve conforming to either IS : 3224-l 979 `SPecification for valve fittings for compressed gas cylinders excluding liquefied petroleum gas ( LPG ) cylinders ( second revision )' or to any other specification approved by the statutory authority. 7.2 It shall have a suitable protection for the valve. Filling 8.1 Vdhile filling, the cylinder shall be filled in such a manner that the filling ratio does not exceed I.1 9 [ see IS : 3710-1978 Specification for filling ratios for low pressure liquefiable gases contained in cylinders ( first revision j 1. 8.2 The amount of liquefied sulphur dioxide charged into each cylindershall be determined by weighing after the cylinder has been disconnected from the line and on no account the cylinder shall be charged in excess of the filling ratio. 8.3 All the cylinders shall be carefully examined for leaks after filling. Where stopped, the cylinders shall be emptied and inspected for the cause of leakage. 8.4 Emptying the cylinder shall not be accelerated in an approved filling by direct heating of the cylinder. station only. ~8.5 Cylinders shall be filled leaks cannot be

IS : 8198 ( Part 9 ) - 1988 EXPLANATORY NOTE
For safe handling of cylinders containing liquefied sulphur dioxide, one should be thoroughly conversant with the properties and characteristics of sulphur dioxide. There are several precautions and safe practices which are to be observed on account of the nature of the sulphur dioxide and also-because of the pressure to which the cylinders are subjected. Manufacturers, fillers and users of the gas cylinders covered by this code should be familiar with the precautions laid down in this code in order to ensure safe and efficient operating condiFor general information on different gases conveyed in cylinders, SP: 9-1973 `Technical tions. data sheet for gases conveyed in cylinders' may also be referred to. The Committee responsible for preparation of this This standard was first published in 1980. standard decided to revise it to bring this standard in line with the development made in the field of gas cylinder technology at the international level. Other Indian Standards published Part 1 Part 2 Part 3 Part 4 Part 5 Part 6 Part 7 Part Part Part Part 8 10 11 12 Atmospheric Hydrogen gases gas in this series, which have a,lso been updated, are as under:

High pressure liquefiable gases Dissolved acetylene gas Liquefied Liquefied Ammonia petroleum gas ( LPG ) chlorine gas gas gases

Common organic refrigerant Methyl bromide gas Methyl chloride gas Gases for medical use

Manufacture, possession and use of any gas, when contained in cylinders in a compressed or liquefied form is regulated under the Gas Cylinder Rules, 1981 of the Government of India as amended from time to time. Although the code has been prepared in consultation and agreement with the statutory authorities under these rules, should anything in the code conflict with the provisions of Gas Cylinder Rules, the latter shall be adhered to. The quantities in this standard have been expressed in technical metric units. However, in view of the introduction of international System ( SI ) units in the country, the relevant SI units and the corresponding conversion factors are given below for guidance: 1 kgf(cm2 = 98'066 5 kPa ( kilopascal of IS : 2432-l ) = O-980 665 bar 963 `Specification for liquid sulphur dioxide' shall

In using this, requirements be borne in mind.
